summary: Interlude client protocol revision 746 is negotiated at runtime: the game client sends protocol integer 746 in its first GameServer packet (ProtocolVersion), and the L2J Mobius CT_0_Interlude server accepts it via config AllowedProtocolRevisions = 746, replying with a KeyPacket that carries the Blowfish/XOR session key and a 1 (accept) / 0 (reject) flag. The local client in C:\Agentic\Lineage2_Interlude_Client is a genuine Interlude client (GameGuard/npkcrypt present, ini files carry the "Lineage2Ver413" cipher header), but the 746 revision is not stored in any readable client file; it lives in L2.exe and is only observable on the wire. The single most important finding for L3: L2J Mobius already ships TWO production mechanisms that run FULL Player objects in the world with a null GameClient and no socket at all -- OfflineTraderTable (offline private stores) and OfflinePlayTable (offline auto-play/botting). Both simply call Player.load(charId) + spawnMe() + setOnlineStatus(true) at server startup, and OfflinePlayTable additionally re-arms AutoPlayTaskManager so the clientless player keeps fighting and moving. This is the exact, clean hook for injecting 5000 synthetic players that bypass the network layer entirely. They do NOT need to speak the packet protocol; the protocol only matters for the ONE real client used during development to verify the server boots and behaves.
key_facts: Client protocol revision 746 (0x2E9) is what the Interlude game client announces to the GAME server (not the login server). Confirmed in L2J Mobius CT_0_Interlude: dist/game/config/Server.ini sets 'AllowedProtocolRevisions = 746', and gameserver/network/clientpackets/ProtocolVersion.java checks the received version against ServerConfig.PROTOCOL_LIST.

Handshake reply: ProtocolVersion.java sends 'new KeyPacket(client.enableCrypt(), 1)' on accept (1 = OK, initializes the packet cipher key) or 'new KeyPacket(client.enableCrypt(), 0)' on reject, and logs 'Wrong protocol version'. A version of -2 is a C2 ping and is disconnected immediately.

The LOGIN server uses a SEPARATE protocol constant: loginserver Init packet writes protocol revision 0x0000c621 plus a scrambled 128-byte RSA modulus (0x90 field), four fixed GameGuard integers (0x29DD954E, 0x77C39CFC, 0x97ADB620, 0x07BDE0F7), and a Blowfish key sent in plaintext before encryption is active. Do not confuse 0xc621 (login) with 746 (game).

Login flow packet sequence (LoginServer): server->client Init (session id, RSA key, Blowfish key, GG constants) -> client->server AuthGameGuard -> RequestAuthLogin (RSA-encrypted credentials) -> server LoginOk -> RequestServerList -> ServerList -> RequestServerLogin -> PlayOk (session keys). Handoff: client reconnects to GameServer carrying those session keys.

GameServer flow (clientpackets): ProtocolVersion (746) -> KeyPacket -> AuthLogin (validates PlayOk session keys against LoginServerThread) -> CharSelectionInfo -> CharacterSelect -> EnterWorld. CharacterSelect.java calls 'Player cha = client.load(charSlot)' then 'cha.setClient(client); client.setPlayer(cha); cha.setOnlineStatus(true, true)'.

Interlude packet cipher is NOT Blowfish on the game stream (that name is legacy). gameserver/network/Encryption.java is a custom stateful running-XOR: encrypt does 'out = raw ^ key[i & 0x0F] ^ prev' with feedback on the previous ciphertext byte; a 16-byte key; and after every packet the key's bytes [8..11] are advanced as a little-endian int by the packet size (the 'dynamic key'). The first outbound packet (KeyPacket) is sent in clear and only enables the cipher. (Blowfish/RSA are used at the LOGIN server only.)

Packet structure: 2-byte little-endian length prefix, then 1-byte opcode, then body. Reads use little-endian primitives (readC/readH/readD/readS UTF-16 strings); writes mirror with writeC/writeH/writeD/writeS. Opcodes are dispatched in GamePacketHandler.java keyed on ConnectionState (CONNECTED/AUTHENTICATED/ENTERING/IN_GAME).

DEFINITIVE HOOK -- clientless Player objects already exist in production: data/sql/OfflineTraderTable.java restores offline shops at startup with 'Player.load(charId); player.setOnlineStatus(true,false); player.spawnMe(x,y,z); player.setPrivateStoreType(type); player.setOnlineStatus(true,true); player.broadcastUserInfo()'. NO GameClient is created and NO socket is opened; getClient() stays null.

data/sql/OfflinePlayTable.java goes further: it restores auto-play (bot) characters with the same load+spawnMe pattern, then 'player.setOfflinePlay(true); player.setRunning(); AutoPlayTaskManager.getInstance().startAutoPlay(player); AutoUseTaskManager.getInstance().startAutoUseTask(player)'. Proves a null-client Player can actively fight, move, and use skills purely server-side.

GameClient has 'private volatile boolean _isDetached = false' with setDetached/isDetached. Entering offline mode calls client.setDetached(true); the write path treats a detached/absent connection as a no-op so the world never blocks on a dead socket. Player holds 'private GameClient _client' and getClient() can legitimately return null (EnterWorld.java guards 'if (player.getClient() != null)').

EnterWorld.java shows what 'entering the world' actually requires vs. what is just client courtesy: PURE WORLD STATE (needed for a synthetic player) = setConnectionState is cosmetic, spawnMe(x,y,z) registers into World object store + region grid, skill add/remove, siege/vitality/instance state, setEnteredWorld(). CLIENT-ONLY (skippable when there is no socket) = every player.sendPacket(UserInfo/ItemList/ShortcutInit/QuestList/FriendList/etc). Only broadcastUserInfo() (state seen by OTHER players) matters for synthetic players.

L2J Mobius CT_0_Interlude ALSO ships a built-in 'FakePlayer' feature, but it is the WRONG model for L3: managers/FakePlayerChatManager.java + FakePlayerData drive NPC objects (org.l2jmobius.gameserver...Npc) that merely display as players and answer whispers via CreatureSay. They are not real Player instances and cannot level, gear, or party like players. L3 wants the OfflinePlay pattern (real Player, null client), not the FakePlayer-NPC pattern.

Client-side version evidence in C:\Agentic\Lineage2_Interlude_Client: system\ contains GameGuard.des + npkcrypt.dll/.sys/.vxd (nProtect GameGuard, an Interlude-era anti-cheat), L2.exe (495 KB launcher stub, protocol constant not in plaintext -- it is packed/GG-protected). The ini files (l2.ini, user.ini) begin with the literal marker 'Lineage2Ver413' and l2.int with 'Lineage2Ver111'; these are the INI/dat CIPHER versions, NOT the network protocol. No client file stores '746' as a protocol value (the one '746' hit in raiddata-e.dat is coincidental raid data). Confirms a real Interlude client but shows the 746 revision is only observable at runtime on the wire.

Package layout note for L3 developers: this branch uses 'org.l2jmobius.gameserver.entity.actor.Player' (confirmed via CharacterSelect.java imports), NOT the 'model.actor.instance.PlayerInstance' path used by other/older L2J forks. Player.load(int objectId) is a static factory that builds a fully-populated Player from the DB rows; it takes an object id, not a client.
architecture_notes: The 5000 fake players must be PURE server-side Player objects that bypass the network layer entirely. Do NOT run 5000 real TCP clients, do NOT implement the packet protocol for them, and do NOT use the client's L2.exe. The protocol (746, KeyPacket, XOR cipher, login RSA/Blowfish) is relevant ONLY for the single real developer client used to smoke-test that the server boots, that a human can log in, and that synthetic players are visible and behave plausibly to that one real client.

The cleanest injection hook is a new 'L3FakePlayerManager' modeled directly on OfflinePlayTable.restoreOfflinePlayers(): for each synthetic character do Player.load(charId) (or a fabricated in-memory Player), setOnlineStatus(true,false), spawnMe(x,y,z), setRunning(), then register with the L3 AI scheduler. Client stays null forever. This reuses code paths Mobius already trusts in production, minimizing NPE surface.

Because getClient() is legitimately null for these players, all outbound sendPacket calls collapse to no-ops -- so a synthetic player costs nothing on the network side. The ONLY packets that matter are the ones OTHER (real or synthetic) players would need to SEE state changes: those go through broadcastPacket/broadcastUserInfo to the KNOWN-LIST of nearby players, and a real client observer receives them normally. Synthetic observers can have broadcast-to-them short-circuited for performance.

L3 should NOT adopt Mobius's FakePlayerChatManager/Npc-as-player model -- it cannot level or gear. It SHOULD adopt/extend the OfflinePlay + AutoPlayTaskManager path, replacing the naive AutoPlay combat loop with L3's tiered AI (Tier 0 rules on a fast task-manager tick, Tier 1 utility planning, Tier 2 batched LLM calls). AutoPlayTaskManager already demonstrates the correct pattern: a shared scheduled task iterating a registered-player collection, so 5000 agents are ticked by a small thread pool, never one-thread-per-player.

spawnMe() is the true 'enter world' boundary for a synthetic player: it inserts the Player into the World singleton object store and the spatial region grid so AI, other players, and geodata see it. Everything else in EnterWorld.java that is a sendPacket to self can be skipped for clientless players. This keeps per-agent entry cost to roughly a DB load (or a synthetic in-memory build) plus a grid insert.

For 5000 agents, prefer synthesizing lightweight Player objects in memory over 5000 real DB rows loaded via Player.load. Player.load pulls many joined tables (items, skills, shortcuts, quests, henna, recipes). L3 should build a slimmer construction path that populates only the fields the AI and broadcast need (position, appearance/CharInfo fields, level, class, HP/MP, name), while still registering into World + region grid so real clients render them correctly.

State a synthetic player minimally needs to be seen by a real client: object id, name/title, position and heading, appearance (race/sex/class/face/hair, visible equipment graphic ids), level, HP/MP, PvP/karma flags. That is exactly the CharInfo/UserInfo payload. As long as these fields are populated and the player is in the region grid, the real observer client renders and interacts with it as a normal player.
risks: The '746 revision only observable at runtime' means the exact wire behavior of THIS specific client build (in C:\Agentic\...) is unverified against Mobius until a real login is attempted. Interlude clients vary in minor packet quirks; Mobius CT_0_Interlude targets the mainstream 746 client and almost certainly matches, but this must be smoke-tested with the real client before trusting the rest.

GameGuard (npkcrypt/GameGuard.des present in the client) can block or crash the real client if the server doesn't send the expected GameGuard auth exchange. Most private-server setups either run a Mobius build with GG checks disabled or patch the client to skip GG. This only affects the ONE real dev client, not the synthetic players, but it can block dev smoke-testing.

Synthetic Player objects created without going through the normal login/AuthLogin path skip account/session validation and several init side-effects. If L3 fabricates Players in memory (not via Player.load from a real DB row) some subsystems that assume a DB-backed char (mail, clan, olympiad, auto-save) may NPE or try to persist garbage. Auto-save in particular (PlayerAutoSaveTaskManager) must be disabled for synthetic players or pointed at a separate lightweight store.

The null-client no-op assumption relies on Mobius's write path tolerating a detached/null connection. This is proven by OfflineTrader/OfflinePlay running in production, but any custom L3 code that calls player.getClient().something() without a null check will NPE for synthetic players. All new code touching synthetic players must null-guard getClient().

Scale unknown: OfflineTrader/OfflinePlay are designed for tens-to-hundreds of idle shop/bot characters standing still, NOT 5000 actively-pathfinding, combat-taking, socializing agents. spawnMe + region-grid + AI-tick + broadcast for 5000 moving players is a different order of load (broadcast fan-out, geodata pathfinding, aggro scans) and is the main feasibility risk for the whole L3 concept -- must be load-tested, likely with aggressive interest-management/LOD so distant agents are simulated abstractly.

Data-pack / client-server content mismatch: if L3 alters items, skills, or map coordinates server-side, the synthetic players are unaffected but the real observer client will render wrong/invisible items unless its .dat files (itemgrp, weapongrp, etc. present in system\) match the server. This is a client-patching concern for the dev observer, not the agents.

License: L2J Mobius is GPL. Any L3 code that links against or derives from Mobius (including the fake-player subsystem built on OfflinePlayTable) is subject to GPL. This constrains distribution and must be reconciled at the project level.
recommendations: Build the L3 fake-player subsystem as a new manager patterned on data/sql/OfflinePlayTable.java: load or synthesize Player, setOnlineStatus(true), spawnMe(x,y,z), setRunning(), register into the L3 AI scheduler. Never create a GameClient or socket for them. This is the single cleanest, lowest-risk injection point.

Reuse the AutoPlayTaskManager pattern (shared scheduled task over a registered-player collection, ticked by a small ThreadPool) as the skeleton for the Tier-0 AI loop, but replace its combat picker with L3's tiered brain. Do NOT spawn a thread per agent.

Keep the network protocol strictly on the dev-observer critical path only: stand up the Mobius CT_0_Interlude server with AllowedProtocolRevisions=746 unchanged, patch/disable GameGuard for the dev client, and verify one real 746 client can log in and SEE synthetic players moving. Treat that as the milestone-1 acceptance test.

For synthetic players, short-circuit self-directed sendPacket entirely (guaranteed no-op since client is null) and, for performance at 5k, also short-circuit broadcasts whose only recipients are other synthetic players -- only broadcast to region cells that contain at least one real client or an agent whose state a real client can observe.

Give synthetic players a slimmer construction path than full Player.load: populate only position, appearance (CharInfo fields), level/class, HP/MP, name/flags, and register into World + region grid. Disable PlayerAutoSaveTaskManager for them and persist L3 agent state through L3's own store, not the per-char DB path.

Null-guard every getClient() access in new L3 code and add an isFakePlayer()/isSynthetic() flag on Player so subsystems (mail, olympiad, clan, auto-save, HWID/anti-feed, disconnect handling) can cleanly opt synthetic players out.

Do NOT use Mobius's built-in FakePlayer (NPC-impersonating-player) feature for the 5000 agents; it cannot level or gear. Reserve it, if at all, only as a fallback for extreme-distance LOD 'ambient crowd' where no real interaction is expected.

Validate scale early with a load test: spawn 500 -> 2000 -> 5000 synthetic Players doing real movement+combat and measure region-grid/broadcast/pathfinding cost with one real client watching, before committing to the 5k target. Plan graceful degradation (fewer fully-simulated agents near players, abstract simulation far away).
open_questions: Does L3 want synthetic players persisted as real DB character rows (so they survive restarts exactly like OfflinePlay/OfflineTrader and can be observed with full fidelity) or synthesized in-memory each boot (lighter, but needs a slimmer construction path and its own persistence for agent memory/relationships)?

What is the real per-agent cost at 5000 for active movement + combat + broadcast on the target hardware, and what interest-management/LOD scheme keeps it inside the tick budget? (This is the make-or-break number for the whole project and was not measurable from source alone.)
Will the dev/test setup patch the client to bypass GameGuard, or run a GG-disabled Mobius build? This gates whether the one real observer client can connect at all.

Does the specific Interlude client build in C:\Agentic\Lineage2_Interlude_Client match Mobius CT_0_Interlude's 746 packet expectations exactly, or will minor client-specific packet quirks need patching? (Needs a live login to confirm.)

How should synthetic players interact with subsystems that assume a live client or account (olympiad, clan wars, mail, party/command channel, siege registration) -- fully participate, or be gated out per-subsystem?
